title: What every part of the Barça crest means
sources: Cross of Saint George / Sant Jordi, patron saint of Catalonia; Sant Jordi's Day 23 April (roses and books)
Senyera: arms of the Counts of Barcelona / Crown of Aragon
Joan Gamper founded FC Barcelona on 29 Nov 1899; FC Basel colours is one popular theory of the blaugrana origin (hedged in the script)
Crest design chosen in a 1910 competition, won by Carles Comamala (medical student, Barça player)

scenes.text: You've seen this crest a thousand times. But do you know what every piece of it means?
Top left: a red cross on a white field.
People often ask why Barça put England's flag on their badge. It has nothing to do with England.
It's the Cross of Saint George, Sant Jordi in Catalan: the patron saint of Catalonia, the knight who slays the dragon in the legend.
Every April 23rd, on Sant Jordi's Day, people in Barcelona give each other roses and books.
Top right: red stripes on gold.
That's the Senyera, the flag of Catalonia. It goes back to the Counts of Barcelona and the medieval Crown of Aragon.
That's why Barça captains wear its colours on the armband, and why the stands are full of it.
At the bottom: blue and garnet stripes. Blaugrana.
Joan Gamper, a Swiss footballer, founded the club in 1899. One popular story says he took the colours from his old club, FC Basel.
scenes.say: Joan Gamper, a Swiss footballer, founded the club in eighteen ninety-nine. One popular story says he took the colours from his old club, FC Basel.

scenes.text: And right in the middle, an old leather ball, because it all started with a love of the game.
The design was chosen in a 1910 competition. The winner was Carles Comamala, a medical student who also played for Barça.
scenes.say: The design was chosen in a nineteen-ten competition. The winner was Carles Comamala, a medical student who also played for Barça.

scenes.text: So next time you see it, remember: a saint, a homeland, a club, and a ball. Visca Barça!
